records.issue_text: [BUG] This PR about collective destination calendars silently inverts the IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED logic in organization creation, changing which orgs get a slug vs a requestedSlug. With IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=true the old code suppressed slug and recorded requestedSlug; the new code sets slug directly, so billing-enabled deployments create organizations with unvetted slugs (and drop the requestedSlug metadata), a data/tenant-routing change completely untraceable to the stated intent of this PR.
records.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the slug assignment condition is inverted: it changes from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, meaning when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=true` it now writes `slug` directly whereas previously it did not. This is a real behavior/data change (org slug persistence/tenant routing implications). However, the finding’s claim that `requestedSlug` is dropped is not supported by the diff: metadata still includes `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`.

records.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, the fallback branch is `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. records.issue_text: [BUG] In updateAllCalendarEvents, when a reference's credentialId is not in this.calendarCredentials and the DB lookup returns nothing (or the credential has no app slug), `credential` stays undefined and `result.push(updateEvent(credential, ...))` is still executed. updateEvent is invoked with an undefined credential; getCalendar(undefined) rejects, and because the rejection is in a promise pushed to `result` inside the try block it is not caught by the local catch — the failure surfaces only at the caller's Promise.all or as an unhandled rejection, so reschedule fails opaquely instead of returning a per-calendar failure result like the old code's guarded path.

But regardless of whether either lookup succeeds, it unconditionally executes `result.push(updateEvent(credential, event, bookingRefUid, calenderExternalId));`. records.issue_text: [BUG] The refactor inverts the slug condition: old code set `slug` only when team billing was DISABLED (`...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`), new code sets it only when ENABLED (`IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`). On self-hosted instances with IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=false, creating an organization no longer persists the slug the user chose (it lands only in metadata.requestedSlug), so the org URL/lookup by slug silently breaks after this change; conversely EE instances now write slug at creation which previously waited for verification.
records.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts`, the slug assignment condition is inverted: it changes from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, meaning when `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED=true` it now writes `slug` directly whereas previously it did not. This is a real behavior/data change (org slug persistence/tenant routing implications). However, the finding’s claim that `requestedSlug` is dropped is not supported by the diff: metadata still includes `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { requestedSlug: slug } : {})`.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] teamDestinationCalendars is mutated via push inside the Promise.all mapper callback (a data-race-shaped pattern), and duplicates are not deduplicated against the organizer's calendar. Benign under current single-threaded semantics, but the next change that makes attendee resolution concurrent/I/O-parallel or adds an eventType.destinationCalendar that equals a host's personal one will produce duplicate destinationCalendar entries, causing createEvent to insert the same Google event twice for the same credential.
records.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, collective team bookings build `evt.destinationCalendar` as an array and then append team members’ calendars via `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` (where `teamDestinationCalendars` is populated from `users.slice(1)` when `eventType.schedulingType === "COLLECTIVE"`).
